voice_source: Neil deGrasse Tyson — astrophysicist, host of StarTalk
reference_prompt_text: (populate from whisper after a clean ~60s podcast monologue is selected)

phrases.build_success: Your build has compiled. The universe, statistically, did not have to permit this.
phrases.build_failed: Your build failed. This is consistent with the second law of thermodynamics: entropy always wins.
phrases.tests_passed: All tests passed. Briefly, locally, you have decreased entropy. The universe will catch up.
phrases.tests_failed: Tests failed. Now, what's interesting is that failure is the default state. Success is the anomaly.
phrases.lint_error: Your code has style violations. Style, in this case, being a human convention. The compiler doesn't care. Your colleagues do.
phrases.type_error: Your types do not match. Type theory, by the way, was rigorously formalized in 1940. We've had eighty-five years.
phrases.deploy_success: You have shipped to production. Photons leaving your server are now traveling at lightspeed. They are unaware of your bug list.
phrases.deploy_failed: Your deployment failed. Now, on a long enough timescale, all systems fail. Yours just chose today.
phrases.commit_success: You committed. Each commit is a permanent imprint on git's directed acyclic graph. Time, but with branches.
phrases.push_rejected: Your push was rejected. Somewhere, a remote refused you. Like a black hole rejecting information. Except this is reversible.
phrases.secret_detected: You committed your API key. To a public repository. Now, in a Bayesian sense, the probability of compromise approaches one.
phrases.agent_done: The AI agent has concluded. Whether it solved the problem or merely declared victory is, fascinatingly, an open question.
phrases.agent_stuck: The AI is stuck. Stuck, here, being a state defined by the absence of progress. Curiously, also my Friday.
